challenges.name: derived-state-quiz
challenges.title: Copy or compute? Read the catalog's state
challenges.description: Three pieces of evidence from the catalog: a filtered list that missed a new course, a details panel after a rename, and a Profiler measurement someone wants to fix with useMemo.

questions.explanation: False. The argument of useState is only the initial value: React uses it on the first render and ignores it afterwards. filterCourses does run on every render (it is an ordinary call in the component body), but its result is thrown away, so the state keeps the 19 courses it started with. DevTools shows the proof: the prop has 20 entries and the state has 19, so the fresh data did reach the component. The fix is to delete the state and compute `const visible = filterCourses(courses, filter)` during render. The misconception is that the expression inside useState(...) keeps the state up to date because it is evaluated each time.

True. selectedId ("c_12") did not change, but `selected` is computed during render from the current props, so this render finds the new object with the new title and passes it to CourseDetails. There is no copy to keep in sync. Had the component stored the whole course (setSelected(c)), the state would still hold the old object with the old title. The common misconception is that you need an effect watching `courses` to update the selection; looking up by id during render makes that effect unnecessary.

questions.question:
The fixed CourseResults computes the list during render:

const visible = filterCourses(courses, filter);

Measured on the production build with 4x CPU throttling:

console.time -> filterCourses: 0.07 ms (120 courses)
React Profiler -> CourseResults render: 0.9 ms

In review, a teammate comments: "Wrap it in useMemo with [courses, filter]."

Statement: "The teammate is right that useMemo is needed: recomputing derived data on every render is what made the earlier version show stale results."
questions.explanation: False, on both counts. The stale results came from copying the list into useState, where it stopped following the props; recomputing on every render is what fixes that. useMemo is a performance cache for a computation, not a correctness tool, and 0.07 ms is far below the roughly 1 ms at which react.dev suggests memoizing is worth considering. Adding it here buys nothing measurable and adds a dependency list that can go wrong: with [filter] alone, a refetched `courses` array would be ignored and the stale bug would return. The misconception is that derived values must be cached to be correct.
